title: Apocalypses and Apocalyptic Writing
lead: Apokalypsis means "unveiling." Scholars use "apocalypse" for a kind of Jewish and Christian writing popular from about 200 BC to AD 100, in which a seer is shown heaven's view of history through visions, symbolic beasts, numbered periods and angel guides. Daniel 7–12 and Revelation are the Bible's main examples; the "Isaiah Apocalypse" (Isaiah 24–27), 1 Enoch, 4 Ezra and 2 Baruch are related.
